pages.name: Direction D — matched to your reference

annotations.text:
DIRECTION D — matched to houseofiqf.com

That site is a stock Shopify Dawn theme with photos swapped in. So the target isn't a bespoke look — it's the standard Indian D2C register: announcement bar, MRP struck through on every card, trust strip, category tiles, reviews, dark footer.

This is that register, for womenswear. No scarcity messaging: normal size runs, normal stock, cards that carry price and MRP and nothing else.

Earlier directions A–C are on the second page.

THE ONLY TIMER LEFT

14:38 on the product page and in the mobile buy bar. It appears ONLY once the item is actually held in that shopper's bag — it is information about their own cart, not a nudge, and a shopper who hasn't added anything never sees it.

It exists because the shop and the site sell from one stock room. That stays true at any quantity; it just stops being something customers need told.

MOBILE

Majority of your traffic. Sticky buy bar carries price and the hold timer, so it stays visible while they scroll.

No fake status bar drawn — the real one renders on top.

All tap targets 44px or larger.

STILL TO DECIDE

1. Cash on delivery. The reference offers it and most Indian D2C does. Now that stock will carry real quantity, a refused COD is ordinary logistics rather than a lost week on your only copy — so this gets much easier to say yes to. Still worth deciding deliberately.

2. Discount depth. The reference runs 30–50% off MRP on everything. Your schema auto-sets sale price at MRP − 10%, so every item shows a genuine 10% off. Deeper headline discounts, or stand behind the 10%?

3. Sizes. These boards assume S–XXL runs. Tell me the real size grid and I'll fix the selectors.
